name: Hanoi food guide
summary: Pho in the Hoan Kiem lanes in the morning, bun cha at lunch, egg coffee in the afternoon, then snail noodles, young rice from Vong, sticky rice, and the rooms that cook in another register: a seasonal Vietnamese menu, a Japanese counter, Cantonese, and the white tablecloths at the Metropole.
body: Eat Hanoi from the bowl outward. The morning soup is pho. Lunch is bun cha. The afternoon sit-down is egg coffee, strong robusta under a sweet egg foam, in the Nguyen Huu Huan alley. Around those three, the city still cooks bun dau, cha ca finished at the table, shrimp cakes that take their name from West Lake, and a breakfast roll of steamed rice.

Around them sit snail noodles, pillow cakes, young rice from Vong, sticky rice, crab noodles, and fresh beer. Walk the street the dish belongs to and read the board. When you want a room instead of a stool, the kitchens run from a seasonal Vietnamese menu and a Japanese counter to Cantonese cooking and the white tablecloths at the Metropole. Hue’s bun bo is the bowl for the day you leave town.
specialtiesLead: Start with pho, bun cha, and egg coffee, then bun dau, cha ca, banh cuon, banh tom, bun thang, and the bowls and snacks around them.

sections.heading: More Hanoi dishes
paragraphs: Papaya with beef jerky, mixed rice noodles, braised chicken noodles, a fried cheese stick, fish balls, fresh beer, beef rolls, young-rice sweets, duck noodles, and the cone on Tràng Tiền.

spots.name: Nom bo kho
spots.note: A sweet and sour plate of green papaya, carrot, and beef jerky. One version adds crunchy peanuts; another adds lemon balm and fish sauce.

spots.name: Banh da tron
spots.note: Thick, flat rice noodles topped with sausage, fried fish cakes, tofu, peanuts, and leafy vegetables. Thin glass noodles are the other option from the same baskets.

spots.name: My ga tan
spots.note: Braised chicken with egg noodles. Regular chicken or the smaller black-skinned bird is simmered in an empty drink can with herbs that include mugwort, then the noodles go into the stew.

spots.name: Pho mai que
spots.note: A fried cheese stick, sold with bánh gối.

spots.name: Ca cuon thit
spots.note: A fried fish ball stuffed with pork, with fresh greens, a light fish sauce, and calamansi.

spots.name: Bia hoi
spots.note: Fresh draft beer, unpasteurized and drunk soon after it is made, as light as water.
spots.address: Tạ Hiện and Lương Ngọc Quyến

spots.name: Pho cuon
spots.note: A roll of fresh rice-noodle sheets, usually the sheets cut for phở rather than dried rice paper, wrapped around grilled beef. Dip it in fish sauce with chili and calamansi.

spots.name: Che com
spots.note: A sweet soup made from young green rice.

spots.name: Cha com
spots.note: A pork patty made with young green rice.

spots.name: Bun ngan
spots.note: A noodle soup of bamboo shoots and duck meat, one of the bowls around Quần Ngựa in Ba Đình.
spots.address: 63 Cửa Bắc, Quán Thánh, Ba Đình

spots.name: Ice cream
spots.note: An ice-cream cone for the evening walk around Hoàn Kiếm.

sections.heading: International dining
paragraphs: Three foreign kitchens sit beside the Vietnamese steak in the French style on Hòe Nhai.

spots.name: Crystal Jade Palace
spots.note: Cantonese cooking from a Singapore kitchen that has served Chinese food in Vietnam for 25 years.

spots.name: Kappou Ishia
spots.note: A Japanese omakase of 10 courses: appetizers, sashimi, a main, rice, and a dessert, chosen by the chef. One credit spells the room Kappou Ishida.

spots.name: Hibana by Koki
spots.note: A 14-seat teppanyaki counter in the basement of Capella Hanoi. Chef Hiroshi Yamaguchi cooks abalone, spiny lobster, sea urchin, Yaeyama beef, and Hokkaido hairy crab. One MICHELIN Star, retained in the 2025 selection.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: The casual city is the morning street, the lunch street, the alley coffee, and the bia hơi corner at Tạ Hiện and Lương Ngọc Quyến.
Đồng Xuân is the covered market in the lanes. Entry is free. It is the shopping hall beside the food.

spots.name: Hang Vai
spots.note: The morning pho street, with the lanes around Hoàn Kiếm.

spots.name: Cua Dong
spots.note: The lunch street for bun cha. Put the noodles in with the herbs. Nem is optional.

spots.name: Ma May
spots.note: The bun dau lane in the Old Quarter.

spots.name: Duong Thanh
spots.note: The cha ca street.

spots.name: Cafe Giang
spots.note: The afternoon alley for egg coffee. Café Giảng is the door.

spots.name: Ta Hien corner
spots.address: Tạ Hiện and Lương Ngọc Quyến
spots.note: The bia hơi corner north of the lake. Stools, draft beer, and the street.

spots.name: Dinh Cafe
spots.note: Second floor of an old French house looking onto Hoàn Kiếm, a classic cafe.

spots.name: Pho Co Cafe
spots.note: A cafe at 11 Hàng Gai.

spots.name: Pho Co Rooftop Cafe
spots.note: A rooftop over the tube houses, with a view of Hoàn Kiếm.

spots.name: Nola Cafe
spots.note: A gallery on top, looking down into the oldest house on the street.

spots.name: Ha Thanh Mansion
spots.note: A century-old villa of three floors, new to the 2025 Bib Gourmand list.

spots.name: Hang Dao night market
spots.note: On weekend nights Hàng Đào becomes a market for snail meatballs, grilled quail, and cured pork sausage.

spots.name: Dong Xuan
spots.note: The covered market in the lanes. Entry is free.

spots.name: Pho Bo Lam
spots.note: Beef heel muscle, with tender meat and gelatinous tendon. New to the 2025 Bib Gourmand list.

spots.name: Pho Au Trieu
spots.note: On the 2024 Bib Gourmand list, on a street parallel to St Joseph’s Cathedral. The broth is cloudy, fatty, and thick, in the Nam Định style, and the shop can sell out. Go early.

spots.name: Bun Cha Huong Lien
spots.note: In 2015 Barack Obama and Anthony Bourdain ate here. The table may have been put behind glass. On the 2025 MICHELIN Selected list.

spots.name: Tuyet Bun Cha 34
spots.note: A 2024 Bib Gourmand room near Trúc Bạch, Trần Quốc, and Quán Thánh. Generous noodles, grilled pork, and herbs.

spots.name: Cha Ca Thang Long
spots.note: Fish cooked at the table.

spots.name: Banh Cuon Ba Xuan
spots.note: Breakfast banh cuon. On the 2025 MICHELIN Selected list.

spots.name: Mien Luon Chan Cam
spots.note: Nearly 40 years in the Old Quarter. Eel cold or stir-fried, vermicelli soup, congee, and spring rolls. New to the 2025 Bib Gourmand list.

spots.name: Mien Luon Dong Thinh
spots.note: More than four decades of glass noodles with eel, greens, crushed peanuts, and fried shallots. A Bib Gourmand.

spots.name: Mau Dich So 37
spots.note: A rustic room for Hanoi spring rolls, fried hemibagrus, and scorched rice with beef stew. New to the 2025 Bib Gourmand list.

spots.name: Uu Dam
spots.note: A vegetarian menu, traditional and balanced. New to the 2025 Bib Gourmand list.

spots.name: Oc Di Tu
spots.note: Prawns, clams, and cockles in a plain room, including melo melo snails with scallion and fried garlic, and Venus clams with lemongrass, chili, and pineapple. On the 2025 MICHELIN Selected list.

sections.heading: Fine dining
paragraphs: Hanoi’s one-star rooms in the 2025 MICHELIN selection are Gia, Hibana by Koki, and Tầm Vị. Lamai Garden received the city’s first Green Star the same year. Spices Garden is the Metropole dining room. A weekend buffet lunch there is 780,000 VND.

spots.name: Gia
spots.note: Vietnamese contemporary cooking. The menu changes with the seasons and draws on Vietnamese culinary heritage. The plates lean on acidity and texture. One MICHELIN Star, retained in 2025.

spots.name: Lamai Garden
spots.note: Reimagined in 2022 by chef-owner Hieu Trung Tran. A seasonal tasting menu and a vegetarian menu, contemporary Vietnamese and farm-to-table. Diners walk a garden to a counter by the open kitchen. Ingredients come from the restaurant’s Phú Thọ farm: herbs, ducks, and black pigs. A squid noodle is inspired by phở chua. MICHELIN Green Star, 2025.

spots.name: Tam Vi
spots.note: Northern Vietnamese cooking in a vintage tea house, with old furniture and handwritten signs. Chả ốc comes with herbs, vegetables, rice vermicelli, and fish sauce, and there is a clear crab soup with malabar spinach. One MICHELIN Star, retained in 2025.

spots.name: Spices Garden
spots.note: The Metropole dining room. Bun cha, pho, and cha ca are cooked with European technique and served on white tablecloths. The weekend buffet lunch is 780,000 VND.

sections.heading: Themed dining
paragraphs: Chim Sáo is a French villa where the staff dress in old peasant clothes and the cooking is home food.

spots.name: Chim Sao
spots.note: A French villa. The staff dress in old-style peasant clothes and the food is home cooking.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Breakfast is pho in the Hoàn Kiếm lanes, banh cuon across the city and at Bánh Cuốn Bà Xuân, bun thang, and xôi mặn, the savoury sticky rice. Phở cuốn is the grilled-beef roll on Ngũ Xã, by Trúc Bạch, in the evening. Bun cha is almost only lunch.

seoTitle: Hanoi food — pho, bun cha, cafes, and fine dining
seoDescription: Morning pho in the Hoan Kiem lanes, bun cha at lunch around Cua Dong, egg coffee in the Nguyen Huu Huan alley, and the other bowls Hanoi cooks.
